newsitem.title: NORWAY: FOCUS - Nycomed profit slips, cutting costs.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Nycomed profit slips, cutting costs.

text.p: Norwegian drugs group Nycomed ASA on Thursday reported a 32 percent drop in nine-month pre-tax profits and unveiled a programme to slash costs by 600 million crowns per year from 1998.
Under a scheme dubbed Focus '98, Nycomed said it would adjust group strategy to reduce costs in some areas and increase investment in others, while strengthening core activities.
Despite the slide in profits, the stock market reacted positively to the restructuring news. Nycomed's A share jumped more than eight percent, or seven crowns, to 90 crowns on the Oslo bourse.

"This is what the market has been waiting for," said one broker. "Restructuring, cost-cutting and a refocus. The market is bullish on this. In the short run we see potential of (a share price of) 100 crowns."

The pharmaceuticals company, one of the largest in Scandinavia, has been under pressure to rethink strategy since June when it warned that intensive competition in the North American market for diagnostic contrast agents would have a severe impact on group revenues in 1996.

"In the short term, the aim of Focus '98 is to lessen the effect of the price fall in the American market, which will have a full impact on earnings in the second half of 1996, as well as to offset expected increased costs from the launch of new therapeutic products," a company statement said.

Nycomed booked profits before tax of 898 million crowns ($140.7 million) in the nine months to September 30, compared with 1.32 billion a year earlier. Operating profits sank 30 percent to 1.04 billion crowns from 1.49 billion.
Third-quarter operating revenues slipped seven percent to 1.8 billion crowns from 1.95 billion, while the three-month profits before tax tumbled almost 50 percent to 220 million from 406 million.
Nycomed blamed the decline on lower sales in the United States of its main X-ray contrast agent product Omnipaque.

"Sales of Omnipaque in the USA were lower than in 1995, mainly due to intense price pressure. This new price level has had an impact on Nycomed's third-quarter earnings and is the main reason for the income decline compared with 1995," it said.
Revenues in the therapeutics area were on a par with 1995, adjusted for the sale of the group's cosmetics business in May 1995.

Nycomed said Focus '98 would not interfere with innovative research in medical imaging. The programme aimed to cut expenses by 150-170 million crowns in production, 110-140 million in marketing and sales, 40-60 million in administrative services, 180 million in research and development and 60-80 million in the U.S. operations.
The company will reduce its workforce by 600 to 700.
Nycomed said between 50 and 70 percent of the anticipated savings were expected to be achieved in the accounting year 1997 with the full effect visible in 1998.
Accrued costs due to the programme were put at about 700 million crowns, of which writedowns of balance sheet items and restructuring costs would account for about 50 percent each.
The company took costs of 14 million crowns in its third-quarter accounts for measures implemented in the first half of 1996. ($1=6.383 Norwegian Crown)
